outputs.title:0: Maren Hassinger Won’t Be Weighed Down
outputs.excerpt:0: Her retrospective at the Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive (BAMPFA) highlights the artist's love of metal and motion.
outputs.block:0:text:0: Maren Hassinger’s retrospective at the Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive (BAMPFA) has a radiant warmth about it—surprisingly so, given that it’s a show made mostly of gray metal sculptures whose edges could prick you raw. This warmth owes a lot to the photographs, printed mural-sized and filling vitrines, taken by her long-term collaborator Adam Avila. Scattered throughout, they show Hassinger dancing, beaming, and/or hamming it up for the camera, often mirroring her sculpture’s forms with her body. But it owes, too, to the ways she rose to meet her career’s surprising twists and turns.
